title: NL coast: THE 80 g/h RATE TEST, flat + hip block
terrain: firm wet sand at the waterline or road, flat, no D+. Dunes are out, national park
coachNotes:
EXECUTION: 1h50 flat on firm wet sand at the waterline or road. No dunes, the park is off limits. Cadence 165-170 spm throughout, strict in the 35min block. Turn around every 10-15min so the right leg is not on the low side of the camber.
GYM, REPLACING THE DUNES: hip abductor block, the one gym intervention with real evidence for ITBS. Side-lying hip abduction 3x15/side, clamshells 3x15/side, single-leg glute bridges 3x12/side, side plank with top-leg abduction 3x30s/side, Copenhagen planks 3x20s/side, single-leg calf raises 3x15. Still no step-downs, split squats or lunges: they load the 20-40 degree flexion band that is symptomatic again.
FUEL, THE RANKED OBJECTIVE OF THE DAY: 80 g/h = 2 Enervit Carbo Gel C2:1 Pro per hour. This is 1h50, so gels at minute 30, 60 and 90, each with 150-250ml water. No SiS gel on top, it is maltodextrin only and breaks the glucose ceiling. Sodium 500-700 mg/h: check the Bulk tub for mg per scoop, it likely needs 2-3 scoops per 500ml. Write down grams, product, and what the stomach did.
STOP RULE: no symptoms during, after, or next day. If the knee speaks, cut to 60min flat and keep the intake.
WHY IT CHANGED: dunes are unavailable, so this window now has no eccentric descent exposure at all, and the hip block does not replace it - 13 days is too short to build descent durability either way. What still pays is the fuelling rehearsal and holding CTL near 42. At 96h post-shockwave the analgesic cover is thinning, so today's knee report is the honest one and it decides how much of the 5 Sep rehearsal gets restored.
